problems: Day 20 (Cavafy, Ithaka): the note assigns the wordings to the wrong editions, as far as this critic can tell from memory (web access to the Cavafy Archive and Poetry Foundation was blocked, so this is unverified). The 1975 Keeley and Sherrard Collected Poems reads hope the voyage is a long one, and the 1992 revised edition, which the Poetry Foundation prints, reads hope your road is a long one. Either keep the voyage wording and cite the 1975 edition, or keep the 1992 citation and change the quote to hope your road is a long one; the editor must check one of the two printed texts before it ships.

Days 20, 29 and 31 mark verse line breaks with a slash inside the quotation, while days 3, 8, 16 and 23 run the lines together as prose with commas; pick one convention for the month, and if the slash stays, the day 29 note about line breaks marked is then also needed on days 20 and 31 or on none.

Day 19 (Dostoevsky): the quotation carries an em dash (new story—the story), which Garnett prints, so it is honest, but it is the only dash on any card this month; confirm the card renders it and that the house voice tolerates it, or cut the quotation at the first clause: But that is the beginning of a new story.

Day 10 (Chekhov) and day 29 (Eliot) carry notes that are context rather than hedge or correction (day 10 explains that the line is not the last exchange; day 29 explains that four verse lines are printed): the rule allows a note only on a hedged or corrected line, so either recast each as a correction of the popular claim in one sentence or delete it.
